title: Check the cast instead of suppressing the warning

blocks.text: The page's `unsafeCast` returns `(List<String>) obj` under `@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")`. The cast checks nothing about the elements, so a list holding `42` gets through and fails later, wherever `get()` meets the `Integer`. The page's advice is to suppress only a warning you have justified, and otherwise to fix the underlying issue.
Write `Casts.strings(Object obj)`, which needs no suppression at all:

items: `obj` must be a `List`: anything else, **a `Set` included**, is refused with `IllegalArgumentException`.
**Every element is checked at the call**: an element that is not a `String` (or is `null`) is refused with `IllegalArgumentException` before anything is returned.
The result holds the same strings in the same order and is **a copy**: later changes to the source list do not reach it.

cases.says: strings() of a list holding "a" and "b" returns a list equal to [a, b].
A list holding "a" and 42 is refused at once with IllegalArgumentException, not later when 42 is read.
A String and a Set of strings are both refused with IllegalArgumentException.
Changing the source list after the call does not change the returned list.

concepts: An unchecked cast to List<String> verifies none of the elements, so checking them fixes the issue a @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") would only hide.
